static_traits.name: Zhang Sining
static_traits.family_status: The youngest child in the family, with older siblings; due to long-term comparison with the older siblings, family relationships have become strained
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; has not received psychological counseling before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, relatively good logic, able to self-reflect; high cooperation, positive attitude; slightly nervous at the first session but willing to cooperate with recording and exercises

basic_info.main_problem: I have always felt I can never surpass my older siblings and am destined to be a failure.
basic_info.core_demands: I noticed that these persistent feelings of inferiority are affecting my self-esteem and overall mental health, so I sought counseling; I want to learn how to challenge these thoughts with concrete steps and apply strategies in real life.
growth_experiences: Beginning in adolescence, the client formed feelings of inferiority and inadequacy, whose core source was comparing their own achievements with those of older siblings; as the siblings reached important milestone achievements, this comparison and inferiority persisted and worsened. It was especially triggered when the family discussed achievements, gradually causing strained relationships with family members; this is the first time the client has sought professional help for this problem.

special_situations.event: Learning that the older sister received a major promotion/achievement at work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not achieve accomplishments equal to or greater than my older siblings', it proves I am inferior to them and a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Downplays or avoids own achievements when communicating with family, reducing talk of career development to avoid comparison
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never succeed like her

special_situations.event: At family occasions, discussing each other's achievements and career development
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not meet the family's expectations or my older siblings' level, I will disappoint them, showing that I am not capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Stays silent at gatherings, avoids talking about personal performance, and lowers presence to reduce being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am no good, that I have let my family down

special_situations.event: Facing new or more challenging tasks at work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a task cannot be completed perfectly or performance is not as good as others', it equals failure and proves I am not capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding new tasks; lowering challenges to avoid possible failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely fail; I had better not take this task

special_situations.event: Reviewing one's achievements in creative projects and receiving some recognition
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only success in the traditional sense, recognized by the family (such as promotion, titles), has value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negates or belittles own achievements in the creative field, continuing to measure the self by others' standards

core_conflict.wish: Desires to be truly seen and recognized by family and significant others, affirmed as an independent individual rather than defined by comparison
core_conflict.fear: Fears failure and being belittled, worrying about being slighted for not being as good as older siblings and losing value and belonging
defense_goal: Reduces the chances of being compared and judged by avoiding challenges and downplaying self-presentation
Keeping topical distance from family to maintain a sense of safety and fragile self-esteem
Internalizing external success standards to gain a sense of certainty, temporarily relieving anxiety

object_relations.self_representation: The 'younger sister' who is inferior and needs to prove herself
object_relations.object_representation: Judgmental, more accomplished, and strict-standard family members/older siblings

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When counseling focuses on 'the standard of success' or invites them to affirm their own achievements and worth
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to regard the success standards of the outside world and family as the only yardstick (transference: internalizing the family's judgmental nature as a universal rule)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Cites external standards in a calm and rational tone (such as 'everyone thinks real success is promotion / titles'), downplays their own achievements, weakens personal feelings and value; avoids entering the level of emotional experience.

manifestations: Completely binds self-worth to family / societal standards of success, believing that different types of achievement 'do not count as real success'
Difficulty gaining a sense of meaning and satisfaction from personal achievements in work and life
Family relationships strained due to comparison
Stays in contact with friends but has not shared the true inferiority and troubles, tending to bear them alone

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treating family/society standards of 'traditional success' as the only correct measure
Negates and devalues one's own achievements and recognition in the creative field

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Restricting action with self-labels such as 'failure' and 'will never surpass'
Avoids challenging tasks at work due to self-blame

positive_force: Has ability in creative projects and has received external recognition
Willing to seek help and cooperate with treatment; positive attitude and able to self-reflect
Has some willingness for reality testing (willing to record and challenge automatic thoughts)
Having several friends who can talk about general matters, having a potential support network
negative_force: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, mind reading and disqualifying the positive
Introjecting external standards of success as the sole basis for self-judgment
Avoids challenges at work, causing further damage to confidence
Ruminative thinking affects sleep and life satisfaction

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding taking on new or challenging tasks at work
antecedent: Facing new or more challenging work tasks
Hearing or seeing colleagues'/older siblings' promotions and achievements being discussed
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by catastrophizing and all-or-nothing thinking, worried that once imperfect or inferior to others it proves they are a failure; long-term comparison with older siblings solidified into a pattern of self-negation
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential failure and external judgment, reducing anxiety and shame in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Work performance and development are restricted, self-confidence declines, further reinforcing the belief of self-failure

target_behavior.behavior: Disturbed sleep (difficulty falling asleep / insomnia due to ruminative comparison and expectation of failure)
antecedent: Reflecting at night on siblings' success and one's own shortcomings
On the eve of work setbacks or facing new tasks
target_behavior.core_reason: Excessive comparison of self-worth and predictions of future failure; negative automatic thoughts ruminate persistently in search of a sense of certainty
target_behavior.function: Attempts to gain a sense of control and explanation through repetitive thinking, temporarily avoiding directly experiencing uncomfortable emotions
target_behavior.consequence: Sleep quality declines, daytime functioning and enjoyment of life decrease, and anxiety and self-negation intensify
